originality.rationale: The final claim is implication-covered by prior primary results plus routine mollification/distribution theory. Guo--Xiao Theorem 1.1 already proves the pointwise continuous \(o(r^2)\) circular Morera theorem. If \(f\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}\) satisfies the audited local \(L^1\)-center hypothesis and \(f_\varepsilon=f*\rho_\varepsilon\), then on every smaller compact set \(J_r f_\varepsilon=(J_r f)*\rho_\varepsilon\) and \(\sup|J_r f_\varepsilon|\le\|\rho_\varepsilon\|_\infty\|J_r f\|_1=o(r^2)\). Guo--Xiao therefore makes every mollification holomorphic, and \(f_\varepsilon\to f\) in \(L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}\) gives the claimed holomorphic representative. Moreover, Zalcman's 1973 Theorem 2 proves the general test-function/Taylor mechanism connecting scaled mean-value measures with weak constant-coefficient PDEs for low-regularity data, so the more precise distributional kernel limit is also a standard specialization of prior machinery rather than an independent new theorem.
